This guard verifies that the investigator has correctly identified the email validation logic in the Go Transit checkout form and accurately reported its location and current behavior.
__PERSONA_PREFIX__The investigator has claimed that case-sensitive email validation occurs in CheckoutForm.tsx around line 306, with related types in CheckoutFormProvider.tsx and types.ts, and that test files exist under src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/__tests__/. These specific claims must be confirmed against the actual repository state before the implementer writes the fix.
__SEAM__This seam catches drift in line numbers, function names, or file reorganization. It ensures the investigator's references are current and that the claimed validation rule and type locations actually exist with the structure described.
__RULE__The rule enforces that email and confirmEmail fields must be compared case-insensitively during checkout form validation. Currently the comparison is case-sensitive, causing valid emails with differing case variations (e.g., "User@Example.com" vs "user@example.com") to fail the confirmation check.
__STATEMENT_LIST__Verify each of these claims:
1. The CheckoutForm.tsx file contains a validate rule with email/confirmEmail comparison near line 306.
2. The comparison logic treats the strings as case-sensitive (no .toLowerCase() or similar normalization).
3. Email and confirmEmail field types are defined in CheckoutFormProvider.tsx and/or types.ts.
4. Existing test files under src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/__tests__/ (specifically Checkout.spec.tsx, CheckoutForm.spec.tsx, or CheckoutFormContainer.spec.tsx) can run and provide coverage for the form validation.
5. No other validation occurs at a different level (API, middleware, etc.) that would also need to be fixed.
__MANIFEST__The declared files are: src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/CheckoutForm.tsx for the validation fix, src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/__tests__/ for adding regression test coverage, and CheckoutFormProvider.tsx and types.ts for reference (reading only, not modifying).
__DOC_SECTION__When evaluating the code evidence, pay attention to the exact string comparison operation used (e.g., === or .equals()), any existing case normalization calls, and whether the form validation is synchronous or async.
__EVIDENCE__Verify by reading the actual source code and test files. Confirm line numbers match the current state, check that the comparison is indeed case-sensitive by looking for the absence of .toLowerCase() or .localeCompare() calls, and verify that test files exist and can import the form component. Any mismatch (wrong line numbers, different function signature, case-insensitive logic already present, or missing test files) indicates the investigator's findings need revision.
__STORY_TITLE__Go‑Checkout Page - Email & Confirm Email Case Sensitivity
__STORY_DESCRIPTION__Ticket AMSD-1919 reports that users entering email addresses with mixed case (e.g., "User@Example.com") during Go Transit checkout cannot confirm their email when they re-enter it in a different case (e.g., "user@example.com"), even though both represent the same valid email address. The form's case-sensitive comparison rejects the confirmation as a mismatch. The fix must implement case-insensitive email comparison in the validation rule to accept equivalent emails regardless of case.
__CODEGRAPH_SECTION__Once all investigator claims are verified, the implementer can confidently locate the validation rule, understand its current behavior, add the lowercase normalization, and write a test that proves mixed-case confirmations are now accepted.
